item.title: Tinubu’s reforms favour rich, worsen poverty — Atedo Peterside
item.description: Atedo Peterside, founder of Stanbic IBTC Bank Plc and Anap Foundation, has said President Bola Tinubu’s economic reforms have benefited wealthy Nigerians while worsening the living conditions of millions of low-income earners. Peterside stated this on Monday during an interview on Arise Television, arguing that although upper-middle-class Nigerians had recorded improvements in their investments and incomes over the past three years, poorer households were struggling to afford basic necessities. He said the reforms had not adequately addressed the economic difficulties confronting the majority of Nigerians. “If you’re upper middle class, I can probably show on the blackboard investments in the stock exchange and all that stuff. “I can show on the blackboard that you’re probably better off in the last three years. If you’re a low-income worker, like somebody without much savings and struggling to eat — what 100 million Nigerians have to do, to eat two meals a day and struggling to pay your bills, I can show you that you’re a lot worse off,” he said. Peterside faulted the government for failing to establish adequate social safety nets for poor Nigerians while implementing the reforms. Citing 2025 data from TheCable Index, he said poverty levels varied significantly across the country’s geopolitical zones, with the North-West, North-East, North-Central and South-South bearing a heavy burden. He said only about 12 states and the Federal Capital Territory had poverty rates below 50 per cent. According to him, most of the states with poverty rates below that threshold were in the South-West, alongside Anambra in the South-East and Edo and Delta in the South-South. Peterside said the regional disparities could shape how Nigerians assess the impact of the government’s economic policies. He added that policymakers might not fully appreciate the depth of poverty in some parts of the country because they did not frequently visit affected communities. “High poverty in Nigeria is largely a zonal problem. It is a problem of the North-West, of the North-East, of the North-Central, and of the South-South,” he said. The businessman maintained that the absence of adequate social protection for vulnerable Nigerians remained a major gap in the implementation of the government’s economic reforms. item.title: Sultan a beacon of unity, stability, says Lawal
item.description: Zamfara State Governor Dauda Lawal has described the Sultan of Sokoto, Alhaji Muhammad Sa’ad Abubakar III, as a unifying leader whose wisdom and steady leadership promote stability. Lawal stated this on Monday at the 13th Shaikh Usmanu Bin Fodiyo Week and the 20th anniversary of the Sultan’s coronation, held at the International Conference Centre, Sokoto. The event, themed, ‘Reviving Ethical Leadership and Social Harmony: Lessons from Sokoto Jihad Leaders’, attracted prominent personalities from Nigeria and beyond. In his goodwill message, the governor said the government and people of Zamfara State had drawn inspiration from the Sultan’s wisdom, guidance and leadership, particularly during challenging social and security situations. Lawal congratulated the Sultan on the 20th anniversary of his coronation, describing it as a historic milestone. He also expressed appreciation for the Sultan’s recent presence and support during the coronation and presentation of staff of office to 19 emirs in Gusau, saying it demonstrated his commitment to strengthening traditional institutions in the region. The governor said the legacy of the Sokoto Caliphate transcended geographical boundaries, noting that its values of knowledge, justice, moral discipline, responsible leadership and human dignity remained relevant to contemporary challenges. He urged Nigerians, particularly residents of Zamfara, to draw lessons from the teachings of Sheikh Usmanu Dan Fodiyo in addressing insecurity, poverty, moral decline and youth vulnerability. Lawal called for greater emphasis on peace, justice, education and social responsibility to strengthen communities. Earlier, the Sultan thanked individuals and groups who had supported him during his 20 years on the throne. He also urged religious, traditional and community leaders to intensify efforts towards promoting peace. The post Sultan a beacon of unity, stability, says Lawal appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: Alli vows to surpass Makinde’s eight-year record in four years
item.description: APC candidate unveils ‘Oyo AHEAD’ development blueprint By Adeola Badru The governorship candidate of the All Progressives Congress (APC) in Oyo State, Sharafadeen Abiodun Alli, has pledged to surpass the achievements of Governor Seyi Makinde’s eight-year administration within four years if elected in 2027. Alli made the promise on Tuesday during the unveiling of his manifesto, tagged ‘Oyo AHEAD’ (Itayo Oyo), at Theophilus Ogunlesi Hall, opposite the University College Hospital, Ibadan. He said the blueprint was designed to reposition the state through purposeful leadership, strategic planning, stronger institutions and people-oriented governance. The APC candidate said Oyo State had enormous economic and developmental potential that could be harnessed through deliberate policies and innovative approaches to improve the lives of residents. He said his ambition was to build a state where opportunities would be accessible to all, public institutions strengthened and the impact of government policies felt across communities, irrespective of their location or socio-economic circumstances. “Oyo State has enormous potential, but we must be deliberate, innovative and committed to translating that potential into tangible improvements in the lives of our people,” he said. Alli described Oyo AHEAD as more than a campaign slogan, saying it represented a comprehensive development agenda based on the expectations of residents and the need to accelerate the state’s development. “Oyo AHEAD is not just a campaign slogan; it represents a development agenda anchored on the people’s expectations and the urgent need to move our state forward. “We want an Oyo State that works for everyone, regardless of location, background or economic status,” he said. He said sustainable development required a coordinated strategy to strengthen institutions, stimulate productive sectors, expand economic opportunities and ensure inclusive participation in governance. “Sustainable development cannot be achieved through isolated interventions. We must strengthen our institutions, support productive sectors, create opportunities for our young people and ensure that every segment of society has a stake in the development process,” he added. The APC candidate said restoring Oyo State’s position among Nigeria’s leading states would require purposeful leadership, responsible governance and a development approach that placed residents’ welfare at the centre of government decisions. He said the manifesto contained policies, programmes and strategies to address the state’s development challenges across various sectors. Alli expressed confidence that his proposed four-year administration would deliver measurable results and surpass the achievements of the incumbent government over its eight-year tenure. item.title: Nigeria needs 10% growth to reduce poverty — Peterside
item.description: By Favour Ulebor, Abuja Businessman and former Nigerian Stock Exchange chairman, Atedo Peterside, has said Nigeria’s economic growth rate of about four per cent is inadequate to generate the jobs and investment needed to lift citizens out of poverty, insisting that the country must target annual growth of 10 per cent. Peterside spoke on Tuesday at the second Oxford Global Think Tank Leadership Conference in Abuja, where he identified declining investment, corruption, political patronage and the misuse of public resources as major obstacles to stronger economic growth. He said Nigeria’s investment-to-Gross Domestic Product (GDP) ratio had declined steadily since 1999, despite the optimism that followed the return to democratic rule, when local and foreign investors showed renewed interest in the economy. According to him, investors have been discouraged by an environment where access to opportunities is often determined by political connections, while small and medium-sized enterprises face harassment from regulatory authorities. Peterside called for an economy in which investors could operate without relying on political connections, stressing that public resources must be channelled into productive ventures to achieve the country’s growth ambitions. He warned against celebrating modest economic growth while corruption and the diversion of public funds persisted, arguing that procurement processes could be manipulated to enrich individuals at the expense of development. “Procurement can become legalised theft,” he said, citing inflated contracts and the award of projects to politically connected business partners as practices that undermine the effective use of public funds. Peterside maintained that Nigeria could not move from four per cent to 10 per cent growth without tackling corruption and ensuring that government resources were invested productively. Also speaking, the Emir of Kano, Muhammadu Sanusi II, acknowledged improvements in some economic indicators but cautioned that headline growth figures did not necessarily reflect the welfare of Nigerians. Sanusi said the country’s economic growth of about 4.5 per cent represented progress compared with previous years, but argued that economic performance should be measured by its impact on people’s lives, rather than GDP figures alone. The former Governor of the Central Bank of Nigeria said the depreciation of the naira had affected GDP per capita, making it necessary to consider the relationship between economic growth, currency movements and household purchasing power. He said the economy should also be assessed through access to education, healthcare, nutrition and employment, as well as the distribution of economic opportunities across the country. Sanusi questioned the significance of headline economic figures if poverty, unemployment and hardship remained widespread. item.title: Zamfara APC primary: My mandate cannot be stolen — Kaura
item.description: By Idris Salisu, Gusau Senator Tijjani Yahaya Kaura, who contested the All Progressives Congress (APC) primary election for Zamfara North Senatorial District, has insisted that his mandate cannot be taken away from him. Kaura made the assertion while addressing a press conference at his residence in Kaura Namoda, where he claimed that he had been officially declared winner by members of the primary election committee sent by the APC national headquarters. He alleged that the committee’s chairman was taken to an undisclosed location by some individuals he described as anti-democratic elements. According to the senator, the chairman was abducted and subsequently announced a result declaring Senator Sahabi Ya’u winner, but a majority of the committee members rejected the announcement and jointly declared him winner. Kaura described the alleged abduction as an attempt to undermine democracy, insisting that the electorate would not accept such an outcome. He also dismissed the opposing camp’s claim that Sahabi had been declared winner, describing the announcement as invalid. The senator said APC members had turned out in large numbers to vote for him as the party’s candidate for Zamfara North in the 2027 general elections. He thanked the electorate for the confidence reposed in him and urged political stakeholders to respect what he described as the people’s mandate and the result announced by the committee members. item.title: Goalkeeper Owono breaks down after collision that led to footballer’s death
item.description: By Adegboyega Adeleye FC Andorra goalkeeper Jesús Owono was reportedly left distraught and broke down in tears in the dressing room after the accidental collision that preceded the death of CD Tenerife forward Jesús de Miguel Alameda, with teammates rallying around him to offer support. According to The Sun UK, the 25-year-old Equatorial Guinea international was seen praying and crying following the incident during Monday’s Segunda División match between Tenerife and Andorra. Owono’s knee struck De Miguel’s head and chest as he rushed out to clear a long ball in the closing stages of the encounter. The 30-year-old striker was left motionless on the pitch, prompting distress among players, some of whom were reportedly seen in tears. The goalkeeper was shown a straight red card before the referee abandoned the match in second-half stoppage time. De Miguel was taken to hospital after reportedly suffering a cardiac arrest on the way, with paramedics said to have resuscitated him. Tenerife initially described his condition as “stable but serious” on Monday night, but he died on Tuesday morning. The Sun, citing Spanish newspaper AS, reported that Andorra players showed great concern for Owono during their journey back from Tenerife, with the goalkeeper visibly shaken by the tragedy. Journalist Ivan Alvarez also told COPE radio that Owono had intended to apologise to De Miguel’s family in person before learning of his death. The goalkeeper has reportedly deactivated his social media accounts since the incident and is said to be seeking an opportunity to offer his condolences to the bereaved family before making a public statement. Meanwhile, a judge is expected to open an investigation into De Miguel’s death, although a Canary Islands court source described the incident as an “accidental collision on the playing field”. The source explained that a judicial investigation is automatically opened in cases of deaths not resulting from natural causes, including accidents. Owono is not expected to face criminal sanctions, according to the report, although he could still face sporting disciplinary action. De Miguel’s partner, Maria, and their one-year-old daughter, Carla, were reportedly watching from the stands when the incident occurred. Tenerife have expressed their grief over the striker’s death, while UEFA has announced that a moment of silence will be observed at all its matches this week in his memory. item.title: DSS DG frees four suspected IPOB members, pays N20m compensation
item.description: The Director-General of the Department of State Services (DGSS), Oluwatosin Adeola Ajayi has set free and approved an initial payment of N20 million to four suspects, out of which, each suspect is to receive five million Naira as compensation after being cleared of alleged membership of the proscribed Indigenous People of Biafra (IPOB). Security sources disclosed that the suspects; Emele Uduma Ibe, Berefgagha Appah, Ondokeyilemi Aggry and Oyeinmokebebeton Aggry, were arrested in May 2022, in Sampou and Akeddei communities in Kolokuma/Opokuma and Sagbama Local Government Areas of Bayelsa State. “The Agency established that they had been misled into believing that they would each receive a monthly payment of N100,000 under the Federal Government’s Amnesty Programme, not knowing that they were being lured by a group of IPOB members who are now facing trial,” disclosed one of the sources. While receiving the four, Deji Adeyanju & Partners, Counsel to the suspects, commended the Service for their relentless efforts towards safeguarding Nigeria’s security, particularly acknowledging the DGSS’ genuine attempt at upholding human rights. Furthermore, he noted the high level of hygiene and professionalism within the Service, being the best he has witnessed in over 20 years of interacting with DSS personnel. He reiterated his earlier public statement that President Tinubu made the right choice in appointing Oluwatosin Adeola Ajayi as DSS DG. Expressing gratitude to the DSS boss, Emele Uduma Ibe who spoke on behalf of others, described the day as the happiest of his life, noting that the experience had taught him a valuable lesson which he would share with others. He offered prayers for God’s continued blessings upon the DSS boss and the management of the Service. Recall that upon assuming office in 2024, the DG ordered a review of over 300 inherited terrorism cases. Currently, the DSS panel has been able to decongest its facility to about 100 after thorough investigations, paying over a billion naira in compensation. The DSS boss awarded N20 million and covered the medical bills of a Jos based businessman, who was shot erroneously by service personnel in Plateau State. Chineze Ozoadibe was also compensated with N10 million after she was wrongfully arrested, Sunday Ifedi who was also compensated with 10 million naira after investigation cleared him of ties with IPOB, likewise Kenneth Okechukwu Nwafor was also paid N5 million after investigation absolved him of IPOB allegations. item.title: 2027: Why youth share of voters dropped – INEC
item.description: ….As UniJos wins campus debate finale By Omeiza Ajayi ABUJA: The Independent National Electoral Commission INEC has explained why youths now make up 29.79 per cent of the voters’ register being prepared for the 2027 general election, down from 39.65 per cent in the 2023 register. Chairman of the commission, Prof. Joash Amupitan SAN, gave the explanation on Tuesday at the grand finale of the INEC Campus Debate at the Law Theatre of the University of Abuja. He said the drop does not mean fewer young people are interested in elections, but that many who counted as youths in 2023 have simply grown older. “Some questions have been asked, why has the number reduced compared to what we have in 2023? But the truth of the matter is that there has been progressive migration of the categories of persons that were youth in 2023, they have now migrated into different age groups”, Amupitan explained. He said the register, “which is currently being reviewed through claims and objection,” puts youth representation at 29.79 per cent. The 2023 register had 37,060,399 youths aged 18 to 34, or 39.65 per cent of the 93.4 million registered voters. Amupitan said the debate was part of the commission’s effort to confront voter apathy among young people. “Our plan is to catch them young,” he said. He said earlier outings showed how little many young people know about the electoral process. “When they ask who is the INEC chairman, unfortunately none of them could get it,” he said. The University of Jos won the final, which was held under the theme “Nigeria’s Electoral Process and Democracy.” Bayero University, Kano, came second, the University of Ibadan third, and the University of Nigeria, Nsukka, fourth. Amupitan, who is a University of Jos alumnus, said the judges’ decision could not be faulted. “From the quality of the debate, it was, honestly, it could go either way and they have done justice to it,” he said. He said the judges took a long time to compute the scores. “They were also trying to use technology with their phone making some computations and arithmetics just to ensure that there is accurate delivery,” he said. Amupitan said the result was so clear that no debater or university should think of going to court. “It will be needless for any of the parties or debaters to think of going to court. So that is why we are not establishing any election petition, any tribunal to review what has been done,” he said light-heartedly. He also told the Director of Voter Education and Publicity to keep track of the finalists, saying he would have employed them immediately if the law allowed. “They are not qualified to have been given automatic employment, if not I will have done that by now,” he said. He added that they must first graduate and complete the National Youth Service Corps NYSC. item.title: Police uncover fake dollar operation in Ondo, arrest suspect
item.description: By Dayo Johnson, Akure The Ondo State Police Command has uncovered a suspected counterfeit dollar printing operation in Odigbo Local Government Area, arresting one suspect and recovering three bags of suspected fake United States dollar notes. The operation followed an investigation into an alleged $6,000 currency fraud involving a businessman in Okitipupa. The police said the case began after Yusuf Nasiru, of Sabo, Okitipupa, lodged a complaint on October 28, 2026, alleging that two men, Peter Desmond and Olami Toro, both from Ode-Irele, approached him at his shop on October 25 to exchange dollars for naira. According to the complainant, he handed over $6,000, valued at about N8.6 million, to the men. However, while waiting for the naira equivalent, the suspects allegedly returned the dollars, claiming they did not have enough money to complete the transaction, before leaving. Nasiru later discovered that the returned notes were counterfeit and reported the matter to the police. The Police Public Relations Officer, DSP Jimoh Abayomi, said operatives of the Okitipupa Division commenced an investigation following receipt of the complaint. He said intelligence gathering and technical tracking led the operatives to one of the suspects, Peter Desmond, at Kiniso Village, via Ajue, in Odigbo LGA. “Acting on credible intelligence from community members, operatives raided the hideout on October 29, 2026, believed to be used for producing and printing counterfeit dollar notes to defraud unsuspecting members of the public,” Abayomi said. He disclosed that one suspect was arrested during the raid, while other occupants of the premises escaped through a perimeter fence. A search of the premises, he said, led to the recovery of three bags containing suspected counterfeit US dollar notes and a small wooden box, which had been taken into police custody as exhibits. Abayomi added that the arrested suspect had provided useful information to assist the ongoing investigation. He said the Commissioner of Police, Felix Ohagwu, had directed that the investigation be intensified to apprehend other suspects, establish the full extent of the alleged criminal network and prosecute those found culpable. The command cautioned residents against engaging in suspicious foreign currency transactions with unverified individuals or accepting seemingly attractive exchange offers outside authorised channels. It also advised members of the public to authenticate foreign currencies before accepting them and report suspicious activities to the nearest police station. The police assured residents of their commitment to combating financial crimes and protecting lives and property across the state. item.title: Nigeria’s exports rise 25% in two years — NPA
item.description: By Godwin Oritse The Nigerian Ports Authority (NPA) has said the country’s exports increased by more than 25 per cent in the last two years, attributing the growth to Federal Government reforms and improved collaboration with port operators. The Managing Director of NPA, Dr Abubakar Dantsoho, disclosed this while speaking at the ongoing Annual World Ports Conference in London, organised by the International Association of Ports and Harbours (IAPH). He said Nigeria’s population and economic potential gave it an advantage over other countries in West and Central Africa, adding that recent reforms had also improved cargo throughput at the nation’s ports. Dantsoho said the export growth was not limited to oil and gas but extended to manufacturing and agricultural products, including cocoa, cashew and other raw materials. “Statistically, the exports from Nigeria in the last two years has increased by 25 per cent. And then these are exports that are not mainly only oil and gas. In terms of oil and gas, like I mentioned, we are doing fantastically around that, but then also in the other areas of manufacturing and agriculture, you know, raw materials like cocoa, like cashew and all that. Volumes have increased,” he said. He attributed the growth partly to the partnership between the NPA and major terminal operators, particularly APM Terminals. The NPA chief said the authority had put measures in place to sustain the growth, including the establishment of Export Processing Terminals to facilitate the handling and documentation of export cargoes. He disclosed that about four such terminals were operating in Nigeria, with the NPA collaborating with terminal operators, the Nigeria Customs Service and other relevant agencies to ensure that export cargoes were processed locally and met required standards before shipment. Dantsoho said the reforms had also positioned Nigeria to take greater advantage of the African Continental Free Trade Area (AfCFTA), particularly through increased trade with other African countries. He cited Nigeria’s engagement with Morocco, which he described as a growing manufacturing hub for electric and other vehicles, as an example of opportunities for cooperation. The NPA managing director also attributed Nigeria’s improved performance in global port rankings to increased efficiency, technology adoption and collaboration with industry stakeholders. He said two Nigerian ports featured among the top 20 in the latest World Bank global ports ranking. Dantsoho further disclosed that revenue generated from ports across the country had quadrupled, alongside an increase in cargo volumes. He said the authority was monitoring port performance across West and Central Africa through a regional dashboard, adding that the data showed improvements in Nigeria’s port efficiency as well as progress in countries such as Tanzania and Kenya. item.title: Ondo Amotekun arrests 301 suspects, deploys 1,200 officers
item.description: By Dayo Johnson, Akure The Ondo State Security Network Agency, codenamed Amotekun, says it arrested 301 suspected kidnappers and other criminals between August and October 2026. The State Commander, Chief Adetunji Adeleye, disclosed this while parading 15 suspects, including those allegedly involved in the abduction of a poultry farmer, Afolabi Ajayi, in Imafon community, Akure North Local Government Area, and the killing of a woman. Adeleye also announced the launch of Operation Laafia DanDan, a security initiative aimed at tackling criminal activities during the ember months and yuletide. He said the corps had secured the conviction of 27 suspects, who were either serving various jail terms or fulfilling conditions attached to options of fines. “Across the board, within these months under review, we arrested 301 suspects. Out of these 301 suspects, we have secured conviction of 27 serving various jail terms or fulfilling conditions for those that have option of fine. “Using alternative dispute resolution on many cases, we were able to resolve 102 cases,” he said. Adeleye attributed the achievements to the support of Amotekun ambassadors across the 18 local government areas, intelligence officers, local task forces, vigilantes and personnel of the corps. He said the agency was winding down its previous operation to begin full deployment for the ember months, with intelligence-led surveillance across the state, particularly on major highways, in urban centres and forest reserves. According to him, the new operation will feature increased patrols by Amotekun Rangers in forests, as well as electronic and physical monitoring of identified crime-prone locations. “We have redesigned a scheme whereby we will have a different operation for this period to guarantee safety of lives and property in Ondo State and for those commuting. “We want to reassure the public that the state remains safe as we are determined to continue 24/7 patrol across all major roads, forest reserves and the metropolis,” he said. The commander disclosed that about 1,200 personnel would be deployed across the 18 local government areas, with particular attention to border communities and routes. He also presented a kidnap victim who was recently rescued without payment of ransom. Adeleye said the corps had commenced training and retraining of personnel on arrest procedures and prosecution, adding that suspects whose investigations had been concluded would be charged to court. On the 15 suspects paraded, he said four were arrested for alleged violations of the state’s anti-grazing law, two for breach of law and order, while nine were arrested in connection with kidnapping. He said three suspects linked to the abduction of poultry farmer Ajayi and the killing of the woman had been arrested, adding that they were identified by the victim and had allegedly confessed to the offences. item.title: Okorocha to Uzodimma: Stop insulting judges, appeal up to the Supreme Court
item.description: By Ikechukwu Nnochiri ABUJA — A former governor of Imo State, Rochas Okorocha, whom the court recently declared the authentic candidate of the All Progressives Congress (APC) for the 2027 senatorial election in Imo West, has warned his successor, Governor Hope Uzodimma, to stop what he described as unwarranted attacks on judges. Okorocha, who spoke at the Federal High Court premises in Abuja after signing processes at the registry in connection with the ongoing legal dispute over the senatorial ticket, urged Governor Uzodimma to exercise his right of appeal, even up to the Supreme Court. He also called on the governor to restrain his supporters, whom he accused of continuing to denigrate the judiciary over a lost case. He said: “I listened to the news yesterday and it was so horrible, so terrible, that Governor Hope’s aides, namely his Deputy Chief of Staff and the National Vice Chairman of the APC, could berate a judge, insult a judge. “To use his words, he said the judgment was rubbish and procured, and that the judge should go and look at himself in the mirror. I think that is terrible. And the other one, who is called his Deputy Chief of Staff and whose wife is even a judge, could be insulting the judge because of a judgment. “So, it means that whenever the judgment is for Hope, it is good, but whenever it is against him, the Judiciary is evil. “I think this is very uncivilized. I want him to caution his attack dogs and his people to refrain from insulting judges. It doesn’t represent this nation well, and I feel particularly hurt. “I was made to understand that he has called all his aides, commissioners and everybody to go on the attack. You see, they are doing all that. Can’t he wait patiently and try to get the appeal through? At least the Supreme Court is there. “So it is very shocking and very surprising. I don’t know what they expected: that the judge should have said that the election was held on the 16th for Hope, when the actual date is the 18th? “Or that he would have said that Hope emerged by consensus, which is not true? Or the paper signed only by the Resident Electoral Commissioner (REC) of Imo State and sent to the National Chairman, saying that it was by consensus and that Hope’s election took place two days before the time? “I don’t understand what their quarrel is all about. I want to say once more: let us protect the sanctity of the Judiciary and let us allow justice to prevail in all matters. Hope has been a very big and unusual beneficiary of the court, and I think he should have respected it.” Okorocha challenged Uzodimma to fault his claims in public rather than attacking judges and the Judiciary, adding: “If you (Uzodimma) think any of the things I am saying is not true and that the judgment is not true, Hope should come on television or come and speak. “Why is he (Uzodimma) hiding and using attack dogs here and there to attack judges? item.title: Farmers-herders clashes reduced in Kano — Commissioner
item.description: By Hadiza Yusuf The Kano State Government says clashes between farmers and herders have reduced significantly following the demarcation of 1,270 kilometres of cattle routes across the state. The Commissioner for Agriculture and Natural Resources, Dr Danjuma Mahmoud, disclosed this on Tuesday while outlining the achievements of the ministry. He said the demarcation had helped address recurring disputes between farmers and herders by providing designated routes for the movement of livestock. According to him, the initiative formed part of the state government’s efforts to tackle longstanding challenges in the agricultural sector and promote peaceful coexistence between farming and pastoral communities. “One important problem that I want to reiterate is the intractable problem of clashes between farmers and herders. We have made significant progress in that regard. “Our project provided demarcated cattle routes covering about 1,270 kilometres across the state. That is why you now hear that clashes between herders and farmers have reduced to the barest minimum in Kano State,” he said. Mahmoud said the ministry had also implemented interventions to boost agricultural production, including the rehabilitation of irrigation facilities and the expansion of cultivable farmland. He disclosed that more than 1,200 acres of farmland had been recovered through the clearing of irrigation channels and rehabilitation of canals at major irrigation sites. The commissioner added that the state government, in collaboration with the African Development Bank-supported Agricultural Transformation Agenda Support Programme (ATASP), had recovered more than 200 additional acres for irrigation. He said the government had secured approval to develop 11 mini dams and irrigation facilities across 11 local government areas. “When completed, these projects will provide about 2,000 additional acres of irrigable farmland in the state,” he said. Mahmoud further disclosed that the ministry had completed more than 70 milk collection centres to improve milk handling and storage in pastoral communities. He said the centres were equipped with storage facilities and solar-powered cooling systems to preserve milk before transportation to markets. item.title: Don’t cause crisis in Obi’s camp, OK Movement warns NDC, Obidients
item.description: … As Camp faces setback amid rift By Henry Umoru ABUJA- AS Campaigns have begun ahead of 2027 general elections, the Obi-Kwankwaso (OK) Movement has warned the Nigeria Democratic Congress Presidential Campaign Council and the Obidient Movement not to cause friction in the camp of the NDC Presidential candidate, Peter Obi. Recall that crisis had last month reared its head between the leadership of the party and the support group when the OK Movement unveiled its presidential campaign council and the leadership of the party immediately took a swipe at the development as it rejected the composition of the Campaign Council. The NDC maintained that the role of support groups should be limited to supporting the party and its candidates, rather than assuming the functions of a political party. The OK Movement on its part, resisted the NDC’s position, saying it had a mandate to ensure that Obi and Senator Rabiu Musa Kwankwaso were elected in 2027. This led to strained relations between the two groups. item.title: Defence Minister welcomes reinstated permanent secretary
item.description: By Kingsley Omonobi The Minister of Defence, General Christopher Gwabin Musa (Rtd), on Tuesday welcomed the Permanent Secretary of the Ministry, Mr Richard Pheelangwah, back to office following the lifting of his suspension and his reinstatement by the Federal Government. Musa expressed confidence in maintaining a cordial working relationship with the permanent secretary, stressing the need to build on their existing synergy to advance the ministry’s mandate. Pheelangwah, in his remarks, expressed appreciation for the opportunity to resume duty and pledged to discharge his responsibilities with renewed dedication, professionalism and commitment to national service. A statement by the minister’s Special Adviser on Media, Leah Katung-Babatunde, said the meeting reaffirmed the ministry’s commitment to institutional continuity, effective service delivery and the pursuit of Nigeria’s defence and security objectives. item.title: Insecurity: Borno Police nab 103 suspected criminals
item.description: By Ndahi Marama, Maiduguri The Borno State Police Command has arrested 103 suspected criminals in connection to combat substance abuse, violence, thuggery and other social vices. item.title: EFCC Uncovers Chinese-Operated Illegal Oil Refinery In Ogun
item.description: The Economic and Financial Crimes Commission (EFCC) says it has uncovered an illegal oil refinery allegedly operated by Chinese nationals in the Ogere area of Ogun State. The Commission disclosed that the operation, carried out on Saturday, October 31, 2026, by operatives of its Lagos Zonal Directorate 2, followed intelligence gathering and surveillance on the activities of illegal sludge oil refiners. The development was contained in a statement issued on Tuesday by the EFCC Head of Media and Publicity, Dele Oyewale. The illegal oil refinery allegedly operated by Chinese nationals. X/@officialEFCC According to the Commission, the refinery was deserted when operatives stormed the premises, following an earlier crackdown on four illegal lithium processing plants in the area. However, they discovered waste products from the refining process, as well as underground tanks believed to have been used for heating and processing sludge oil. “Two of the underground tanks inspected contained substances suspected to be Automotive Gas Oil (AGO), otherwise known as diesel,” the statement said. The EFCC said preliminary investigations showed that the operators sourced sludge oil, also known as black sludge, from Warri in Delta State and Port Harcourt in Rivers State before transporting it to the facility in Ogere for processing. The illegal oil refinery allegedly operated by Chinese nationals. X/@officialEFCC It explained that further investigations indicated that the operators subjected the sludge oil to intense heat, allowing lighter petroleum components to pass through a series of chambers and filters in a process believed to produce Automotive Gas Oil (AGO) for sale in the Nigerian market. The Commission added that security personnel at the facility told its operatives that the Chinese operators never disclosed their identities or the name of the company behind the operation. Operatives of the Lagos Zonal Directorate 2 have since taken over the premises as investigations continue to establish the identities of the operators, ownership of the facility and the full extent of the suspected illegal activities and economic sabotage. item.title: High Court Hears Bid To Overturn Australia Social Media Ban
item.description: Australia’s landmark social media ban faces a legal test on Tuesday, as online platform Reddit urges the nation’s highest court to scrap the world-leading restrictions. Social media companies have been forced to purge millions of accounts after Australia banned under-16s from the likes of Facebook, TikTok and Reddit last December. The High Court of Australia will sit on Tuesday and Wednesday as Reddit, one of the most popular websites in the world, argues the laws are misguided and should be overturned. Reddit has highlighted a number of issues in its written submission to the court, pointing to problems enforcing the ban and a lack of scientific evidence about the harms of social media. “The evidence so far is that the effectiveness of the ban has been limited,” reads Reddit’s submission. Australia’s ban works by restricting children under 16 from holding accounts on the world’s biggest social media platforms. Map of Australia These platforms are responsible for weeding out underage users and face hefty fines if they are found to be falling short of their obligations. Reddit argued this approach was actually more dangerous, as registered accounts were governed by in-built safety features. Material posted on many online platforms and social media sites could still be accessed without an account, Reddit said. “Young people using other platforms without an account are also unable to be protected from exposure to particular harmful content as they previously had been,” its submission read. Australia said its restrictions would protect young users from graphic content, online predators and predatory algorithms designed to keep people scrolling. While there is a growing body of evidence about the harms of social media, Reddit argued there was no “scientific consensus”. Political discourse Reddit, which has also argued it should be exempt from the ban, said there was little research on whether certain platforms were safer than others. The High Court will also consider arguments from Australia’s Digital Freedom Project, which believes the ban restricts teens’ ability to take part in political discourse. “Social media is an important means of accessing news and engaging in political communication for young Australians, including children under 16,” the advocacy group argued in written submissions. “The restriction also risks removing beneficial sources of connection, support and participation,” it added. Reddit and the Digital Freedom Project separately announced last year they would challenge the ban. It was not clear how long it would take the high court to consider the case, although even the quickest decisions typically take months. Social media firms face mounting scrutiny over their use of allegedly addictive algorithms and stand accused of directing users to extreme content to keep them scrolling.
